disclosure.title: Thumbwell needs Accessibility to count your reels

points.lock: Shows the lock screen when you hit your limit
points.never: Never reads your messages, never sends screen content anywhere

body.what: To count Reels, Shorts, TikToks and Spotlight videos, Thumbwell uses Android’s AccessibilityService API. While you use Instagram, Instagram Lite, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook, Facebook Lite or Snapchat, it reads screen layout information (which screen is open, the names of on-screen elements, and scroll events).
body.use: We use this only to: count how many short videos you watch, show your count and mascot, and — if you set a limit — cover the reels screen or go back when you reach it.
body.never: What we never do: we do not read or store your messages, comments, video titles or what is in the videos. We do not record your screen. Everything is processed on your phone and is not sent to us or anyone else.
body.off: You can turn this off any time in Android Settings → Accessibility.

disclosure.consent: I understand and agree that Thumbwell uses the Accessibility service as described above.

restricted.title: Allow restricted settings first
restricted.subtitle: Android 13+ blocks Accessibility for apps installed outside Google Play. Do this once:

steps.back: Come back and turn on Accessibility

restricted.openHint: Opens Thumbwell's App info in Android settings

accessibility.title: Turn on Thumbwell in Accessibility
accessibility.path: Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Thumbwell → ON
accessibility.warning: Android will show a scary warning. That’s normal for all Accessibility apps. We only do what’s listed on the previous screen.
accessibility.banking: Some banking or payment apps ask you to pause Accessibility apps while you use them. If one asks, pause Thumbwell — we’ll remind you to turn it back on.
accessibility.successBody: Your Thumbwell can feel reels now.

notifications.title: Let Thumbwell tap you on the shoulder
notifications.subtitle: Limit warnings, streak reminders and a heads-up if counting stops. Max 4 a day.
notifications.examplesLabel: Example notifications: 12 reels left today, your streak is safe, counting stopped

stopped.title: Counting stopped
stopped.body: Tap to turn Thumbwell back on.

battery.title: Keep counting in the background
battery.body: Some phones stop apps to save battery. Then your count stops too.
battery.usage: We use under ~1–2% battery a day (target)
battery.allowHint: Opens Android battery optimisation settings. Choose Thumbwell, then Don't optimise.

oem.title: One more step for your phone
oem.subtitle: {{maker}} phones are strict about background apps. Do these so counting never stops.
oem.vary: Steps vary by OS version · help page has screenshots
oem.failed: Couldn’t open it. Settings → Apps → Thumbwell

samsung.name: Samsung · One UI
steps: Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add Thumbwell
Turn off “Put unused apps to sleep”

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO · MIUI / HyperOS
steps: Other permissions → pop-up windows while in background (only if needed)

oppo.name: Oppo / realme · ColorOS / realme UI
steps: App info → Battery usage → Allow background activity

vivo.name: Vivo / iQOO · Funtouch / OriginOS
steps: Battery → Background power consumption → Thumbwell → Allow
i Manager → App manager → Autostart → ON

oneplus.name: OnePlus · OxygenOS
steps: App info → Battery → Unrestricted / Don’t optimise

pixel.name: Pixel / stock · Android
steps: Battery → Unrestricted (the previous step is enough)

tester.title: Tester setup
tester.intro: Thumbwell counts the short videos you watch (Reels, Shorts, TikTok, Spotlight) so you can see your daily scroll habit. Thanks for testing!
tester.step3: 3. Tap Thumbwell and switch it On, then confirm.
tester.step4: 4. Greyed out? Go to Settings > Apps > Thumbwell (App info) > ⋮ > Allow restricted settings, then try again.
tester.playProtect: Installed from an APK? Google Play Protect may block or warn about it. If so, pause Play Protect scanning in the Play Store (Profile > Play Protect > ⚙), install, then turn it back on.
tester.badgeNote: While testing, a small purple badge shows today's count at the top of the screen when you watch reels.
